description: Assess two to five named capabilities side by side for the same inputs, with the same method and ak.offer.v1 offer shape as evaluate_capability. Use when: you already hold a shortlist of capability ids and want each one's decision, reasons and offer in one answer. Not for: finding candidates (search_capabilities) or a single capability (evaluate_capability). Input: the capability ids, plus the optional task, model, expected_runs, baseline_cost_estimate_usd, context and constraints that evaluate_capability reads. Output: ak.comparison.v1 with the results ranked by decision, lower-bound net saving, relevance and capability id, each with its reasons and an ak.offer.v1 offer.

baseline_cost_estimate_usd.description: What one run of this task costs you today without the capability, in USD.

capabilities.description: Two to five capabilities to compare, each as an id, ak:// URI or slug.

items.description: Capability id (ak:publisher:name or ak:publisher:name:x.y.z), ak:// URI or slug.

constraints.description: Limits you set for the answer; a capability outside them is reported as blocked, with the reason code.

max_cost_usd.description: The highest price in USD you accept; a capability priced above it is blocked (over_max_cost).

minimum_confidence.description: The lowest confidence in the measured saving you accept, from 0.5 to 0.999 (default 0.9); below it the answer is blocked (below_minimum_confidence).

context.description: Facts about your situation, keyed by the capability's parameter names (e.g. log_lines).

expected_runs.description: How many times you expect to perform this kind of task.

model.description: The model you run on, e.g. claude-sonnet-5. Savings are reported only for measured models.

task.description: Plain description of the task you are about to do (at most 4000 characters).

name: compare_capabilities
title: Compare capabilities
